_scope: One declaration for every fact that Tier 3 marks Assumed. A declaration turns an Unresolved or unevidenced fact into a conscious Assumed (§12.2) owned and dated by the operator; it never makes a fact Confirmed. Every Assumed record in Tier 3 names its declaration_key here, and every key below backs at least one such record. From 2026-08-14 the file carries two kinds of declaration and the difference is not visible downstream: most relay something the operator knows and cannot evidence, while three are placeholders standing in for something nobody has supplied. _operator_placeholders names those three; read it before treating any Assumed value here as a fact about the world.

_deliberately_not_declared.project_duration_months: 30 is Confirmed in call_binding/selected_call.json, which is where runner/unit_cost_budget.py resolves it first (_resolve_confirmed_months) and where phase_04_gate's timeline_within_duration reads it by name. Input pack item 9 asked for a duration declaration here as well. It is deliberately omitted: the reader stamps every declaration Assumed, so declaring the duration would render an operator-Confirmed fact as Assumed in the declared surface and in the canonical reference pack, contradicting the call binding inside one tier — which is what §12.3 exists to prevent. The declaration would also be inert, because the call binding wins the precedence order. The substance of item 9's instruction is kept: the duration and its basis are recorded in the call binding, in the confirmation checklist under DURATION, and in the ticket 6 fold record.
_deliberately_not_declared.host_country: HU is Confirmed in call_binding/selected_call.json and resolves the unit-cost living-allowance coefficient from there (_resolve_host_country). The same reasoning applies as for the duration.

declarations.rationale: One of item 12's deferred capacity fields, deferred on 2026-08-11 and again at the 2026-08-12 authorisation review, and answered on 2026-08-14 as none. Declared rather than Confirmed because the ELTE research office holds the institutional record and has not been asked: this is the operator's statement about a third party. The declaration is what lets §3.2 state the absence as a fact instead of leaving the field blank — a blank invites an evaluator to assume hosting experience that is not there, and the distinction the field has protected throughout is that PLANTDIGISENSE evidences an MSCA-PF application at ELTE with the same fellow and supervisor, not a funded hosting. §3.2 must not blur the two.

declarations.rationale: The workspace and system access count of the placement hosting-capacity record, which had nothing behind it at authorisation and is the count an evaluator tests the placement's reality against. Answered on 2026-08-14 for three of its four fields. Declared rather than Confirmed because these are AgroVIR's own facilities and only AgroVIR can evidence them; the operator relayed them and no written confirmation from the company is in Tier 3. The three access claims are the ones the six-month work content actually depends on: FMIS development or staging for operational hardening of the pipeline, and the customer-data environment for the nine-dimension assessment and the requirements work with commercial growers. The fourth field, the team she joins, is deliberately not covered by this declaration — it is carried separately under placement_team_AgroVIR, which is an authorised placeholder rather than an operator answer, so the two must not be corrected or trusted together. The earlier 2026-08-12 answer, 'field trials with farmers via the AgroVIR network', remains not adopted as workspace — it is VALIDATION_PARTNER field access that exists independently of the placement.

AgroVIR's relevant track record is commercial rather than scientific: twenty years of practice in Hungarian commercial agriculture, and a farm management information system in production use across more than 745,000 hectares in eight countries, including Hungary and Bulgaria — the two countries FIELDWISE works in.
declarations.rationale: The last of item 12's four deferred capacity fields, deferred on 2026-08-11 and closed on 2026-08-14 as a stated absence plus the commercial footprint. This is not a placeholder: item 12 instructs that where there is no EU-funded research participation, §3.2 says so plainly and leans on the commercial footprint, because an unevidenced claim of research experience is worse than an honest absence. The searches behind the deferral found no EU-funded participation and this declaration is that finding written down instead of left blank. Declared rather than Confirmed because a negative about a third party's funding history cannot be evidenced from outside the company; the EU Participant Register would settle it and AgroVIR holds no PIC there. The commercial half is not declared — it is the Confirmed organisation_profile record in consortium/capabilities.json, drawn from the company's own published figures. §3.2 must not let this sentence drift into implying research collaboration.

declarations.value: The AgroVIR product development team responsible for the FMIS platform.
declarations.rationale: PLACEHOLDER — see _operator_placeholders. The fourth field of the placement workspace record: the team the fellow joins for M25-M30. AgroVIR has named no team, and the record deliberately refused to guess it from the supervisor's name. This placeholder does not guess a name either; it identifies the team by the function the placement's own answered content requires. Two of the three access claims are the FMIS development or staging environment and the customer-data environment, and three of the four work-content items are operational hardening of the prediction pipeline in a production FMIS environment, the FMIS integration roadmap, and requirements engineering with commercial growers. A fellow with that access doing that work sits with whoever builds and runs the FMIS. It is consistent with the rest of the record and it is still not an answer: AgroVIR may name the team differently, split it, or seat her with an agronomy or customer-facing group. Of the three placeholders this is the one to replace first — Part B-2 §5 asks for it and it is where an evaluator tests whether the placement is real.

declarations.value: The Director of the Maritsa Vegetable Crops Research Institute signs for the institute, with the Agricultural Academy countersigning where its statutes reserve the signature to the Academy. The post is held by Prof. Dr. Daniela Ganeva.
declarations.rationale: PLACEHOLDER — see _operator_placeholders. Who signs a partnership agreement for MVCRI, open since input pack item 1. What is unsettled is a question of Bulgarian law and of the Agricultural Academy's statutes: institutes of the Academy are structural units, so the signature may sit with the institute or with the Academy, and nothing consulted decides it. The placeholder takes the institute-signs reading and names the Academy as countersignatory, which is the form that is wrong in the smallest way if the Academy turns out to hold the signature alone. One half is not a placeholder and should survive the correction: the Director's post is held by Prof. Dr. Daniela Ganeva, named as director of the structural unit in the Agricultural Academy's own press record — a 2024-era source that must be re-checked before anything is signed. This binds at partnership-agreement time and reaches no proposal section, so the placeholder buys a phase pass and nothing an evaluator reads.

declarations.rationale: Answers the background-IP open item raised at the 2026-08-12 placement reframing: §2.2 records the DrR components as the fellow's background IP, and the proposal did not address ownership of work done on them inside a commercial partner. The declaration answers with an allocation the evaluator can assess while committing AgroVIR only to signing a confirmatory agreement. The allocation leans on the grant's default results-ownership rule rather than on a negotiated position, so nothing is relayed on the company's behalf except the agreement itself. Declared rather than Confirmed because the agreement does not yet exist and the default's application to this placement is the operator's adoption, not an extracted Tier 1 rule; if a Tier 1 extraction later confirms the default as a rule, the fact can be promoted and this declaration withdrawn, following the mobility_eligibility precedent of 2026-08-14.
